title: European Convention on Human Rights
summary: Signed in Rome on 4 November 1950 by the members of the newly founded Council of Europe, the convention set out the rights a state may not take from a person — life, liberty, a fair trial, conscience, expression, assembly — and, unusually for a treaty of that date, built machinery to enforce them, ending in a court at Strasbourg that individuals could eventually reach directly. It is the first instrument of its kind with teeth. Portugal, a dictatorship in 1950 and not a member of the Council of Europe, joined both only after the revolution, and the convention entered into force here in 1978.
